summary.headline: SJS Enterprises Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR2,601.2 million (+29.7% YoY) with EBITDA margin at 30.3% and PAT of INR488.7 million.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's strongest quarter on revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with revenue up 29.7% YoY and EBITDA up 53% to INR807.6 million. Management attributed margin expansion of 424 bps to a richer product mix, higher exports and operational efficiencies. FY26 revenue reached INR9,550.7 million (+25.6%) and PAT INR1,718 million (+44.6%), with a net cash position of INR2,437.1 million. Management guided to outperforming the auto industry by 1.5x to 2x in FY27, backed by an order book said to be over 85% of FY27 forecast revenue.

segments.name: 2-wheeler and passenger vehicle (automotive)
segments.commentary: Automotive segment grew 41.1% YoY in Q4 FY26 against industry production growth of 18.9%. FY26 mix: 2-wheeler 38.3%, passenger vehicle 41.7%.

segments.name: Consumer and others
segments.commentary: Contributed around 20% of FY26 revenue. Management said consumer business slowed in Q4 after a product rationalisation at Walter Pack and some orders pulled into Q3 ahead of tariff uncertainty.

segments.name: New generation products
segments.commentary: About 24% of consolidated revenue. Management targets 25% to 30% over the next five years.

guidance_outlook: FY27: expects to outperform underlying industry growth by 1.5x to 2x, versus 2.5x delivered in FY26; management said 1.5x to 2x is consistent with prior guidance.
Exports: target to raise share of consolidated revenue to 14% to 15% by FY28.
Long-term standalone EBITDA margin expectation of 27% to 28% with high growth; internal benchmark above 25%.

Capex: about INR220 crore special initiatives over three years from FY26 plus normal capex of INR15 to 20 crore per year; about INR260 to 270 crore over three years, with INR80 crore spent in FY26. Management said all three special projects should be completed in FY27.
Display business: supplies expected to start early FY28, with the Hosur plant machines arriving by Q2 FY27.
Kit value expected to reach 5x to 8x the DRHP base by early FY28 (display-led).
capex_capacity: SJS Bangalore: utilisation about 75%; INR45 crore expansion adds about 20% capacity; equipment installed and parts shipping, with final modifications due by end of the current quarter.

SDPL (Decoplast, Ranjangaon, Pune): utilisation 95%+; INR100 crore greenfield chrome plating plant in final commissioning, expected to almost double capacity; trials ongoing and customers being signed to book capacity.
Hosur optical display facility: leased, about 97,000 sq ft ready, equipment on order; cover glass about INR40 crore and display about INR25 crore, roughly INR65 crore total.
Management said Bangalore and SDPL spend (INR145 crore planned) was only about INR80 crore incurred so far because payments are milestone-linked; work is ongoing.
demand_pricing: Management said FY26 was a record year for the automotive industry, April 2026 was very strong, and customers are gearing up for high growth.
Input costs: polymer prices are rising with crude, but aesthetic products are repriced annually; chrome plating has back-to-back pass-through with about a one-quarter lag.
Order book is over 85% of FY27 forecast revenue.
New wins cited: Mahindra, Suzuki, Whirlpool, Bajaj Auto, Atomberg, John Deere; FY26 additions included Hero MotoCorp, Autoliv USA, FCA USA, Orafol USA (for Nissan), Yazaki and River.
Display business: partnership with BOE Varitronix (Hong Kong) for optical bonding and assembly; management said the display plan covers cover glass, TFT bonding and, eventually, backlight.
Exports are being developed through sales reps in Turkey, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, South Korea and Germany; management described the global opportunity as about USD 4 billion.

qa_highlights.question: How much of 2-wheeler and PV outperformance is content-led versus market-share-led?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not give a split. Growth comes from new business wins, new higher-value products and higher share at existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Was the 1.5x to 2x FY27 outperformance guidance a downgrade from 2x to 2.5x?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no. The 2.5x in FY26 was specific to large export wins and the Hero program; 1.5x to 2x has been the consistent guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why was consumer business weak in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Walter Pack shed low-margin products, a new higher-value program is in ramp-up, and some Q3 orders were pulled forward to beat tariff uncertainty. Management expects growth to return over the next one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a status update on Bangalore and Decoplast capacity and why is capex below guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Bangalore is in final modifications and Decoplast is in final commissioning. The gap is timing, as payments to contractors are milestone-linked, and capex is expected to complete in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will the display business follow the 5x to 8x kit value target, and what is the BOE scope?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects supplies from early FY28. Phase 1 is optical bonding of TFT with cover glass; Phase 2 is in-house cover glass with coatings; backlight is an ambition. Software is excluded.

qa_highlights.question: Are acquisitions planned, and what is the funding stance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has about INR243 crore available for deployment and is in talks with a few targets in North America, Southeast Asia and India. Deals will be bite-sized, and it is open to some debt for strategic deals.

risks_watch: Consumer and others segment: Walter Pack revenue fell YoY and Q4 was hit by pulled-forward Q3 shipments. Recovery depends on the new ramp-up over the next one to two quarters.
Input cost: polymer and crude-linked increases depend on the annual repricing and the one-quarter pass-through lag for chrome plating.
Capex execution: Bangalore and Decoplast spend was about INR80 crore against about INR145 crore planned; commissioning and payment timing are open.
Display business: the BOE Varitronix tie-up is still pre-revenue, with supply expected in early FY28 and the Hosur machines due by Q2 FY27.
Global macro: management flagged ongoing wars and tariff uncertainty as risks to export and consumer demand.
Margin sustainability: management guides 27% to 28% long-term, below the Q4 30.3% EBITDA margin.
summary.management_tone: Confident and bullish on automotive demand and FY27 outperformance, while openly acknowledging near-term consumer weakness and capex timing gaps. Management was evasive on splitting growth between content and share gains, and on the exact display capex and revenue timeline, which it described as early FY28.
key_quotes: Based on our current strong performance, execution visibility and the current order book being over 85% of the FY27 forecasted revenue, we expect to outperform underlying industry growth by 1.5x to 2x in FY27.
So, we are well aware of that. And we are balancing what we need to do to make sure that we continue our growth trajectory.
So it's just a matter of releasing those payments to get that accounted for. That's it.
